reviews.title: Almost Useless
reviews.text: This app has WAY too many notifications… to the point it is almost useless as I can’t find what I want in all the noise. They send WAY too many email reminders for the same thing… and send alerts to the app at 5:00 AM and on weekends. Very disappointing!!!

reviews.title: 300 hoops to jump through to “join” events
reviews.text: I have fought with this for nearly 40 minutes now, and I cannot get access to the event I have a ticket for; the app won’t let me "join" the event because I never received an invitation code; I cannot edit my registration info to link to a different email even though I signed up less than an hour ago; the desktop version doesn’t work because it insists you use the app; and every time I refresh the page, I’m required to input YET ANOTHER 2FA code. I consider myself a highly tech-savvy person, and every time a conference/convention wants to use this app, I end up wanting to throw my phone out the window. It gets worse every year.

reviews.title: Somewhat annoying
reviews.text: Whova has all the important information but there’s just a ton of extraneous, social media, networking, etc. which can be annoying when it bombard you with messages. Also, it lacks the capability to check off individual talks on your agenda, making it hard to go from session to session.

reviews.title: Virtual meet-ups a virtual disaster
reviews.text:
Our denomination used this app for our General Assembly last year for a face-to-face gathering. Most things worked well. This year we did a mostly virtual version with much of the content virtual “meet ups”. These promised to be very convenient— Whova would handle all the networking. If only it had worked!   Some people were able to get on. Some hosts desperately sent out zoom links. After going 0/2 on virtual meet-ups I pivoted mine to an external link. A third of the people who RSVPed attended. Apparently some were in the Whova meeting that the rest of us couldn’t get to but didn’t get my notice (sent through Whova) that  we were pivoting.

In fairness to Whova a new version rolled out 2/3 of the way through the meeting. It might be better, but the meet-ups are behind us. Frankly, I hope Whova is behind us as well.
